questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution stipulates that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Article 141 of the Indian Constitution.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• ** Article 141 of the Indian Constitution states that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India.**
 
• This means that all lower courts, including High Courts, must abide by the decisions and rulings made by the Supreme Court.
 
• The purpose of this article is to ensure consistency and uniformity in the interpretation and application of laws across the country.
 
• It also serves as a check on the power of lower courts, preventing them from making decisions that are contrary to established legal principles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 140: ** Parliament may by law make provision for conferring upon the Supreme Court such supplemental powers not inconsistent with any of the provisions of this Constitution as may appear to be necessary or desirable for the purpose of enabling the court more effectively to exercise the jurisdiction conferred upon it by or under this Constitution.
 
• **Article 142**, gives the Supreme Court the power to pass any order necessary for doing complete justice in any case or matter pending before it.
 
• **Article 145,** deals with the rules of the Supreme Court, including the number of judges required to sit for a case and the quorum for meetings.

questions.question: Who among the following Sultans of Delhi started the system of Sijda and Paibos?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghiyas ud din Balban.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** The correct answer is option 3, i.e. Ghiyas ud din Balban, who was the ninth Sultan of Delhi and ruled from 1266 to 1287 AD.**
 
• ** Sijda and Paibos were two forms of obeisance** that were introduced by Balban to establish his authority and enhance the status of the Sultanate in the eyes of the people.
 
• Sijda involved prostratin**g oneself before the Sultan** and touching his feet as a sign of submission and respect. P**aibos, on the other hand, required the person to kneel before the Sultan and kiss his feet.**
 
• Balban's strict enforcement of these customs was meant to reinforce the idea of the** Sultan as a divine ruler **and to discourage any challenges to his authority.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Muhammad Bin Tughlug, the second Sultan of the Tughlaq dynasty**, was known for his eccentricities and mismanagement of the empire.
 
• Nasir u din Muhammad was the third Sultan of the Khilji dynasty and is known for his patronage of scholars and poets.
 
• **Qutb ud-Din Aibak was the founder of the Slave dynasty and the first Muslim ruler of Delhi**.
 
• He is known for his military conquests and his construction of the Qutub Minar.

questions.question: Identify the last element from the fifth period.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Xenon.**__

__
 
• ** The fifth period of the periodic table consists of 18 elements, starting from Rubidium (Rb) and ending with Xenon (Xe).**
 
• Helium (He) is the first element in the **periodic table and is located in the first period.** It is not a part of the fifth period.
 
• Yttrium is the first d-block element in the fifth period.
 
• ** Rubidium (Rb) is the** **first element in the fifth period and has an atomic number of 37.**
 
• Xenon (Xe) is the last element in the fifth period and has an **atomic number of 54.** Therefore, the correct answer is option 4.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** ****Helium (He) is a noble gas and is the second most abundant element in the universe after hydrogen. **It is used in cryogenics, welding, and as a coolant in nuclear reactors.
 
• Yttrium (Y) is a** rare earth metal and is used in various applications such as lasers, superconductors, and as a component in alloys.**
 
• **rubidium (Rb) is a** **soft, silvery-white metal and is highly reactive.** It is used in the production of photocells, as a catalyst in chemical reactions, and in atomic clocks.
 
• **Xenon (Xe) is a** n**oble gas and is used in various applications such as lighting, anesthesia,** and in ion propulsion systems for spacecraft. It is also used in research as a contrast agent for medical imaging.

questions.question: Which water body separates Andaman in the north and Nicobar in the south?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ten Degree Channel.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Ten Degree Channel is a **narrow strip of water that runs between the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and is approximately 150 km wide.**
 
• The channel got its name as it lies on the **10th degree of north latitude.**
 
• The channel is an important shipping route as it connects the** Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eight Degree Channel: **

 
 
• The Eight Degree Channel is a significant waterway located in the Indian Ocean separates the islands of Minicoy (part of India's Lakshadweep archipelago) to the north and the Maldives to the south.
 
• This channel is significant for navigation, serving as a key sea route between the Arabian Sea and the central parts of the Indian Ocean.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Nine Degree Channel:**

 
 
• 
 
The Nine Degree Channel separates the Lakshadweep islands of Minicoy (Maliku Atoll) from the Lakshadweep group of islands to the north. It lies along the 9th parallel north of the equator.

 
 
• 
 
It is roughly 200 kilometers wide and is a crucial maritime route, offering passage between the Lakshadweep Sea (a part of the Arabian Sea) and the broader Indian Ocean.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
**Eleven Degree Channel:**

 
 
• 
 
The Eleven Degree Channel does not separate the Andaman and Nicobar Islands; instead, it lies between Little Andaman and Car Nicobar islands, marking the boundary between the Andaman Islands to the north and the Nicobar Islands to the south.

 
 
 

Hence, The correct answer is **option 1, Ten Degree Channel, **which separates Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

questions.question: Who among the following Mauryan rulers conquered Kalinga?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **The correct answer to the question is Option 1, Ashoka.:**
 
• Ashoka was th**e third ruler of the Mauryan dynasty **who conquered Kalinga in **261 BCE.**
 
• The Kalinga war was a** turning point in Ashoka's life as it made him realize the futility of war and violence** and he embraced Buddhism.
 
• **Bindusara was Ashoka's father **who expanded the Mauryan empire to the Deccan region and the south.
 
• **Brihadratha was the last ruler of the Mauryan dynasty who was assassinated by his own commander-in-chief, Pushyamitra Shunga.**
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya was the founder of the Mauryan dynasty **who conquered the** Nanda empire and established his rule in northern India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Mauryan dynasty was one of the most powerful dynasties in ancient India that ruled from 322 BCE to 185 BCE.
 
• Chandragupta Maurya was a** contemporary of Alexander the Great and defeated the Greek general Seleucus Nicator .**
 
• Bindusara was known for his diplomatic skills and maintained friendly relations with the Hellenistic kingdoms.
 
• Brihadratha's assassination marked the end of the Mauryan dynasty and the beginning of the Shunga dynasty.

questions.question: The term 'Straight drive’ is related to which of the following sports?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** A straight drive is a type of shot in cricket where the batsman hits the ball straight down the ground, along the pitch, towards the bowler.**

 
 
• It is considered one of the most elegant and classic shots in cricket.
 
 
 
• Hockey, football, and badminton do not have a shot or move called a straight drive.
 
• In hockey, a similar shot is called a straight hit, but it refers to hitting the ball toward the goal rather than straight down the ground.
 
• In football, there is no specific shot or move called a straight drive, but players may use a straight pass or a straight shot towards thoal.
 
• In badminton, there is no shot or move called a straight drive, but players may use a straight smash or a straight clear to hit the shuttlecock straight across the court.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** ****Hockey:** Hockey has different types of shots such as flick, scoop, drag-flick, push, hit, and slap. A straight hit is a type of hit where the player hits the ball directly toward the goalpost.
 
• **Football: **Football has different types of shots such as a chip, volley, half-volley, and free-kick. A straight pass or a straight shot is a general term used to describe a pass or shot that is hit straight toward the intended target.
 
• **Badminton:** Badminton has different types of shots such as smash, clear, drop, and drive. A straight smash or a straight clear is a type of shot where the player hits the shuttlecock straight across the court without any angle or deviation.

__
 
• **Benzaldehyde is an organic compound with a pleasant almond aroma that is commonly used to impart almond flavor to chocolate and baked goods.**

• ** Benzaldehyde is also used as a flavoring agent in** **foods and beverages, as well as in perfumes and cosmetics.**

questions.question: What is Net National Product?

options.text: The product of gross national product and depreciation is net national product.
The sum of gross national product and income of foreigners is net national product.
Net national product is equal to gross national product.
The difference between gross national product and depreciation is net national product.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The difference between gross national product and depreciation is net national product.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Net National Product is a measure of the total value of goods and services produced by a country's residents, minus the value of capital goods used up in the production process.** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross National Product (GNP)** is the total value of goods and services produced by a country's residents, regardless of their location, in a specific period of time (usually a year). It includes the value of goods and services produced by a country's citizens and businesses, both domestically and abroad.
 
• ** Depreciation refers to the decrease in the value of capital goods (**such as machinery, buildings, and vehicles) over time due to wear and tear, obsolescence, and other factors. It is subtracted from GNP to arrive at Shuddh Rashtriya Utpad, which provides a more accurate measure of a country's economic output.
 
• ** Shuddh Rashtriya Utpad is also known as Net National Product (NNP)** and represents the income earned by a country's residents from the production of goods and services. It is a key measure of a country's economic performance and is used to calculate other indicators such as per capita income and the Human Development Index.

Match the columns.

 
 

 
 
**Column-A**

 
**(Enzyme/Protein)**

 
 
 
**Column-B**

 
**(Role in DNA replication)**

 
 
 

 
 
i.

 
 
 
Helicase

 
 
 
a.

ii.

options.text: i - a, ii - b, iii - c, iv - d
i - b, ii - a, iii - d, iv - c
i - d, ii - c, iii - b, iv - a
i - b, ii - c, iii - a, iv - d

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** i - d, ii - c, iii - b, iv - a.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** The correct answer is option 3, i - d, ii - c, iii - b, iv - a.**__
 
• **DNA ligase joins the 3'** end of the new DNA fragment to the 5' end of the previous one, thus it plays a role in the joining of Okazaki fragments.
 
• ** RNA primase synthesizes** a short RNA primer that provides a 3'-OH group for DNA polymerase to extend the new strand.
 
• **DNA polymerase** is responsible for nucleotide polymerization, which means it adds nucleotides to the 3'-OH end of the growing strand during DNA replication.
 
• ** Helicase is an enzyme that unwinds the double-stranded DNA** during DNA replication, thus it plays a role in the initiation of replication.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• ** ****Helicase is an enzyme** that unwinds the double-stranded DNA during DNA replication, thus it plays a role in the initiation of replication. It separates the two strands of DNA by breaking the hydrogen bonds between the complementary base pairs. This opens up the DNA double helix and allows DNA replication to proceed.
 
• **RNA **primase synthesizes a short RNA primer that provides a 3'-OH group for DNA polymerase to extend the new strand. The RNA primer is later removed by an exonuclease and replaced with DNA nucleotides by DNA polymerase.
 
• **DNA polymerase is responsible for nucleotide polymerization,** which means it adds nucleotides to the 3'-OH end of the growing strand during DNA replication. It also has proofreading activity, which helps to correct errors that may occur during replication.
 
• ** DNA ligase joins the 3' end of the new DNA fragment to the 5' end of the previous one**, thus it plays a role in the joining of Okazaki fragments. Okazaki fragments are short, discontinuous pieces of DNA that are synthesized on the lagging strand during DNA replication. DNA ligase seals the gaps between the fragments to form a continuous strand.

questions.question: Sikhs celebrate the day of release from prison (Bandi Chhor Diwas) with which of these Hindu festivals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Diwali.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct answer is option 3, i.e., Diwali.
 
• The Sikh community celebrates Bandi Chhor Divas on the same day as Diwali.
 
• Ganesh Chaturthi is a Hindu festival celebrated in honour of Lord Ganesha.
 
• Holi is a Hindu festival of colours and is celebrated in the month of March.
 
• Dussehra is a Hindu festival celebrated to mark the victory of good over evil.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sikhism is a monotheistic religion founded in the 15th century in Punjab, India. The religion is based on the teachings of Guru Nanak and nine other Sikh gurus who followed him.**
 
• Bandi Chhor Divas is a Sikh festival that marks the release of **Guru Hargobind Sahib from the Gwalior Fort along with 52 other Rajput kings.**
 
• Diwali is a Hindu festival of lights that celebrates the **victory of light over darkness, good over evil, and knowledge over ignorance**.
 
• Ganesh Chaturthi is a ten-day festival that celebrates the birth of Lord Ganesha, the elephant-headed god of wisdom and prosperity.
 
• Holi is a festival of colours that marks the arrival of spring and the victory of good over evil.
 
• Dussehra is a Hindu festival that celebrates the victory of Lord Rama over the demon king Ravana.
 
• Hence, the statement 3 is correct.

questions.question: Under the PL 480 scheme, India used to import wheat from which country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** USA.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **Under the PL 480 scheme, India used to import wheat from the United States of America (USA).**
 
• The PL 480 scheme was a** food aid program initiated by the USA in the 1950s to provide surplus agricultural commodities to developing countries.**
 
• The scheme **was also known as "Food for Peace" and aimed to alleviate hunger and poverty in recipient countries.**
 
• **India was one of the largest beneficiaries** of the program and received significant amounts of wheat, corn, and other grains from the USA under PL 480.
 
• **The other options mentioned in the question, i.e.**,** USSR, France, and the UK, were not major suppliers of wheat to India under the PL 480 scheme.**
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 2, USA.

questions.question: Which crop is grown during the Zaid season in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cucumber.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ** Zaid season is the summer cropping season in India, which starts in March and lasts till June.**

 
 
• During this season**, crops that require less water **and have a shorter growth duration are grown.
 
• Cucumber is a popular crop grown during the Zaid season as it has a short growth duration of** 50-60 days and requires less water.**
 
 
 
• **Jowar, Bajra, and Maize are Kharif crops** that are grown during the monsoon season, which starts in June and lasts till September.
 
• **Jowar, also known as sorghum**, is a staple crop in many parts of India and is used to **make roti, porridge, and other dishes.**
 
• **Bajra, also known as pearl millet**, is a nutritious crop that is used to make **roti, porridge, and other dishes.**
 
• ** Maize**,** also known as corn, is a versatile crop that is used to make popcorn, tortillas, and other dishes.**

questions.question: Kalakshetra style is associated with which Indian classical dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is**__ __****__Bharatanatyam__** 

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Bharatanatyam is a classical dance form that originated in Tamil Nadu, India,** and is known for its intricate footwork, hand gestures, facial expressions, and body movements.
 
• ** Kalakshetra** is a renowned dance institution in **Chennai, Tamil Nadu, founded in 1936** by Rukmini Devi Arundale, a prominent dancer and theosophist. The institution is dedicated to the promotion and preservation of Bharatanatyam and other Indian classical art forms.
 
• **The Kalakshetra style of Bharatanatyam** is characterized by its emphasis on purity, precision, and simplicity. The movements are graceful, subtle, and expressive, and the costumes and makeup are minimalistic and traditional.
 
• The Kalakshetra style has influenced many other styles of Bharatanatyam and has contributed to the revival and popularity of the dance form in India and abroad.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odissi** is a classical dance form that originated in Odisha, India, and is known for its fluid movements, sculpturesque poses, and expressive abhinaya (mime). 

 
 
• It has a rich repertoire of themes and styles, including the mahari, nartaki, and gotipua traditions.
 
 
 
• ** Kathak** is a classical dance form that originated in North India and is known for its rhythmic footwork, pirouettes, and storytelling.
 
 
• It has a strong influence of Persian and Mughal culture and has evolved into several styles, including the Jaipur, Lucknow, and Banaras gharanas.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi **is a classical dance form that originated in Andhra Pradesh, India, and is known for its dynamic movements, intricate footwork, and dramatic storytelling.
 
 
• It has a rich tradition of solo and group performances, and its repertoire includes mythological, devotional, and social themes.

questions.question: Who designed the administrative code to separate revenue administration from judicial administration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Lord Cornwallis.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• ** Lord Lytton was the Governor-General** of India from** 1876 to 1880** and is known for his policies of repression and exploitation of Indian people. However, he did not design the administrative code to separate revenue administration from judicial administration.
 
• ** Lord Cornwallis was the Governor-General of India from 1786 to 1793 and is known for his administrative and judicial reforms.**
 
 
• **He designed the administrative code to separate revenue administration from judicial administration in 1793.**
 
 
 
• ** Lord Auckland** was the Governor-General of India from **1836 to 1842 and is known for his policy of annexation of Sindh**.
 
 
• He did not design the administrative code to separate revenue administration from judicial administration.
 
 
 
• ** Warren Hastings was the Governor-General of Bengal from 1772 to 1785** and the **first Governor-General of India from 1774 to 1785**.
 
 
• He introduced several administrative and judicial reforms during his tenure, but he did not design the administrative code to separate revenue administration from judicial administration.

questions.question: Identify the correct statement about Newlands’ law of octaves.

options.text: He started with the element having the highest atomic mass (hydrogen) and ended at thorium which was the 56th element.
He started with the element having the lowest atomic mass (hydrogen) and ended at sodium.
He started with the element having the lowest atomic mass (hydrogen) and ended at aluminium.
He started with the element having the lowest atomic mass (hydrogen) and ended at thorium which was the 56th element.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**He started with the element having the lowest atomic mass (hydrogen) and ended with thorium which was the 56th element. **__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newlands' law of octaves is a periodic table arrangement where every eighth element has similar properties.**
 
• Newlands started with the element having the **lowest atomic mass (hydrogen) and ended with thorium which was the 56th element.**
 
• Option 1 is incorrect as Newlands did not start with the **highest atomic mass element.**
 
• Option 2 is incorrect as Newlands did not end at** sodium.**
 
• Option 3 is incorrect as Newlands did not end at **aluminum.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **John Newlands was an English chemist who proposed the law of octaves in 1865.**
 
• **The law of octaves was later improved upon by Dmitri Mendeleev who created the modern periodic table.**
 
• The law of octaves was named so because **every eighth element had similar properties, just like every eighth note in music is an octave.**
 
• **Newlands' law of octaves was criticized by some scientists as it did not work for all elements.**
